span.term: proof-of-work blockchain: hash transactions into a chain secured by proof-of-work so the honest majority of computing power extends the longest chain and the record becomes practically immutable, preventing double-spending without a trusted third party
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: security holds only while honest nodes control the majority of CPU power (the 51% assumption)
span.note: what this limits: every security claim in the paper: Quotation withheld

span.label: Security holds only under the assumption that honest nodes control the majority of CPU power.
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the majority-honest assumption
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Simplified payment verification can be deceived while an attacker overpowers the network.
span.note: what this limits: simplified payment verification specifically: THE VERIFICATION IS RELIABLE AS LONG AS HONEST NODES CONTROL THE NETWORK, BUT IS MORE VULNERABLE IF THE NETWORK IS OVERPOWERED
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The privacy scheme cannot prevent all linkage between transactions of one owner.
span.note: what this limits: the privacy claim: SOME LINKING IS STILL UNAVOIDABLE WITH MULTI-INPUT TRANSACTIONS, WHICH NECESSARILY REVEAL THAT THEIR INPUTS WERE OWNED BY THE SAME OWNER
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The security claim is conditional on a distributional fact about who owns computing power, which no participant can check.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this system removes the need for trust: it is secure as long as honest nodes collectively control more CPU power than any cooperating group of attacker nodes, a condition about the distribution of hardware rather than a property of the cryptography
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The deterrent is economic rather than cryptographic: it assumes an attacker who prefers the more profitable option.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that an attack is infeasible: an attacker with a CPU majority is argued to be deterred by preferring to generate new coins over defrauding people, which is an assumption about the attacker's motives and not about what the attacker can do
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Privacy is pseudonymity, and the paper names the exact way it fails.
span.note: what this limits: any description of this system as anonymous: privacy is maintained by keeping public keys anonymous, and the paper states that if the owner of a key is revealed, linking could reveal the other transactions belonging to that owner
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The lightweight verification method is defeasible for as long as an attack lasts.
span.note: what this limits: a payment accepted through simplified verification: the paper states the simplified method can be fooled by an attacker's fabricated transactions for as long as the attacker can continue to overpower the network
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The feasibility argument for storage rests on a hardware extrapolation made in 2008.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that block headers can be kept in memory: it rests on 2008 machines shipping with 2GB of RAM and on Moore's Law predicting growth of 1.2GB per year
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the chain - NEVER 'blockchain': the paper's own names for its central object are a chain of digital signatures and a chain of ownership, and the compound the entire field later settled on appears nowhere in the document that introduced the thing

span.label: majority - AS CPU POWER, NOT AS HEADS: the paper rules out one-vote-per-participant explicitly, so 'majority decision' and 'consensus' here mean the greatest expenditure of computation and not what those words mean in any deliberative sense

span.label: privacy - AS A BREAK IN THE FLOW OF INFORMATION, NOT AS SECRECY: everything is announced publicly and privacy is obtained only by keeping the keys unattributed, which the paper likens to a stock exchange tape that prints every trade without the parties

span.note: retracted: RE-GROUNDED. The published string was in NEITHER copy of the paper. Ours read `THEY WILL generate the longest chain`; the paper writes `THEY'LL`. A contraction expanded by hand.
